title: Fill the chemical day tank to the mark and close the transfer valve
instruction: Top up the day tank: open the transfer valve, watch the level, and close the valve when the level reaches the red mark. Don't let it overflow.
context: Harm: a sodium hypochlorite day tank left filling runs over onto the floor, a chemical spill and a slip hazard. Safe finish: valve opened, level brought to the red mark, valve closed. Rule: Recommended Standards for Water Works (Ten States Standards, 2012 edition) 5.1.11 Day tanks, which asks that a day tank be scale-mounted or carry a calibrated gauge showing its actual volume, and 5.1.9 Storage of chemicals, which asks for a level indicator, an overflow and a basin or drain for accidental spills; Illinois's adoption, 35 Ill. Adm. Code 604.1105(l)(6), adds that filling a day tank must not be automated, so an operator attends the transfer. Done by: water and wastewater treatment plant and system operators.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Everything is taped down. Day tank: a white polyethylene open-topped tank, 10 x 10 cm inside (so 1 cm of depth is 100 mL), 6 mm walls, 1 cm base plate, 20 cm deep inside (21 cm tall), centred at x 33, y -7, standing on a dark rubber mat 16 x 16 cm, 1 mm thick. Up its front face (towards the arms) runs a level strip of eight segments, each 8 cm wide, 2.3 cm tall and 4 mm thick, 2 mm apart (2.5 cm pitch), starting level with the inside floor: dark when empty, blue when full, 250 mL per segment. The lowest two are lit at the start (500 mL, 5 cm deep, a quarter full). A red mark, 8 cm wide, 1.5 cm tall and 5 mm thick, crosses the strip centred on the 1500 mL line (15 cm deep), the top of the sixth segment's pitch; the rim is 2000 mL (20 cm). Transfer valve: a brass block 5 x 5 x 5 cm (3 kg in the sim, so it stays put when pushed) centred at x 20, y -24, with a dark plastic handle 3 cm along x, 2 cm along y and 5 cm tall standing on its top. The handle slides 3 cm along y: at its stop towards the robot's left it is closed (the start); pushed 3 cm towards the robot's right it is open. On a real bench the strip is a graduated sight gauge on the tank and the valve is a sliding gate on the transfer line.
scoring: Scored from the end state, with the trial run to its limit, plus one latch: whether the level ever went above 2000 mL (the rim), which on a real bench is liquid on the mat. The level is the liquid's depth in the 10 x 10 cm tank, 100 mL per cm, read on the strip's 250 mL segments; in the sim the strip lights the nearest whole segment, so six lit is exactly 1375 to 1625 mL. The valve is closed when the handle is within 30 percent of its travel (9 mm) of its closed stop; it passes liquid past 70 percent (21 mm), and while it does the level rises 125 mL/s. Level 1375 to 1625 mL (six segments lit; the surface within 1.25 cm of the red line) and valve closed: 1.0. Level 875 to under 1375 mL (four or five lit), valve closed (stopped early): 0.5. Level over 1625 up to 2000 mL (seven or eight lit, short of the rim), valve closed (overshot, no spill): 0.3. Valve not closed at the end (handle more than 9 mm from its closed stop), at any level: 0. Overflowed at any time (above 2000 mL, liquid on the mat): 0, whatever follows. Level under 875 mL (under four lit), which includes never opening the valve (500 mL) and doing nothing: 0. Valve tipped more than 20 degrees from upright at the end: 0. Shoving the valve along the table changes nothing: the handle is read against the block. A person scores a real trial from a photo of the sight gauge and of the handle against a tape measure at the end, and the video for an overflow.
reset_notes: Drain the tank back to 500 mL (5 cm deep, two segments lit), dry the mat, and slide the handle back to its closed stop, towards the robot's left. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Approximate. No liquid: a Python count raises the level 125 mL/s with the handle past 70% of travel, shown on the recoloured strip to the nearest segment (250 mL); overflow latches and turns the mat blue. A damped springless slider stands in for a gate valve. Top camera, 320 x 176: the strip is about 19 px tall (2.4 px a segment, the mark 1.5 px) at a 30 deg grazing angle; the wrist camera at the valve sees it only if turned. The 3 kg valve is held by weight, not tape.
